Strait of Hormuz Status: October 11, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  224 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
11 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.42 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera and gCaptain report US forces disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew attempted to run Iran's blockade, with CENTCOM saying no crew were harmed.

02 Splash247 reports attacks on commercial shipping are spreading deeper into the Gulf, with a fully laden VLCC struck off the UAE and another tanker hit in the strait.

03 Tasnim and the IRGC claim a supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz; gCaptain and Anadolu Ajansı also carry the report.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with the conflict now spreading into the wider Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. Al Jazeera and gCaptain report that US forces disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored warnings and attempted to run Iran's blockade; CENTCOM says the ship's stern was struck and no crew members were harmed, reported on October 10. Separately, Splash247 reports that attacks on commercial shipping are widening deeper into the Gulf, citing a fully laden VLCC struck off the UAE and a tanker hit in the strait. Iranian state media, Tasnim, claims a supertanker caught fire after hitting a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz; gCaptain, Anadolu Ajansı, and Deccan Herald also carry the report. Mehr News, Tehran state media, reports a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile on its port side as it was leaving the waterway, a claim gCaptain and Anadolu Ajansı also carry. The IRGC additionally claims an oil supertanker exploded after hitting a mine, per Iranian state media; Anadolu Ajansı reports the same claim. No maritime authority has confirmed the mine account. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the last session before the close; futures are shut. As of 06:20 UTC, 79 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
